subject: Physics
paperTitle: Paper 3 Section B Option D — Turning points in physics
sourceVerification: Each part and marks checked against official June 2022 AQA question paper and final mark scheme; 3.12 topic codes cross-checked against AQA official specification. Source figures inspected visually on question-paper pages 2, 6, 10 and 12.
markingGuidanceOriginalSummary: Question 01.2 is six-mark level-of-response: evaluate three strands together using the official descriptors; do not award full marks from scattered keywords.
Question 02.3 has a dependent second algebra mark; the second cannot be awarded without the first.
Question 02.4 requires evidence of comparison with the elementary charge; arithmetic-error follow-through is restricted.
Question 03.2 allows alternative calculation routes, and a final conclusion consistent with the route used.
Question 04.1 depends on the actual plotted answer choices; no plain-text stand-in is source-equivalent.
Calculation questions permit source-specified valid alternate methods and ECF; contradiction and prohibited statements must be handled before point allocation.
copyrightNotice: Contains independently written skill summaries, topic codes, source references and mark totals only. No original AQA question stems, mark-scheme answers, diagrams or figure content reproduced.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Newton corpuscular model and observed sharp boundaries
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Independent corpuscular/straight-line premise and distinct boundary consequence; interference mentions neutral.
Six-mark level-of-response across apparatus alterations, wavefront/wavelets and phase/path-difference interpretation. Holistic level judgement, not six isolated keywords.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Predictions of competing light models at circular apertures
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Distinguish each theory's prediction and the edge/fringe appearance; accept properly labelled diagram annotations.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Charge polarity and equilibrium in Millikan apparatus
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: One combined mark needs correct polarity and force-field explanation; incorrect viscous-force rationale not accepted.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Stokes terminal-speed model and oil-drop mass
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Separate terminal force balance, density/sphere geometry and evaluated mass; final precision threshold from source.
Second algebra mark depends on correctly established first force equation; method evidence mandatory.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Charge quantisation test using Millikan measurements
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Use relation, compute charge, compare to integer electron-charge multiples; follow-through only under source conditions.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Viscosity measurement error propagated to electron charge
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Track error direction through viscous drag, inferred droplet mass and charge; formula references required for final inference.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Meaning of extinction rotation frequency in Fizeau experiment
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Second mark depends on identifying frequency at absence of return light; distinguish lowest extinction frequency.
Accept maximum measurable speed OR required frequency, with units and consistent feasibility conclusion; limited arithmetic ECF.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Electric and magnetic vacuum constants in Maxwell model
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Distinguish electric field and magnetic flux density roles; generic field labels alone limited.
Original multiple-choice curves must be available; correct option only, no keyword substitutes.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Relativistic speed when kinetic and rest energies coincide
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Separate energy relationship, substitution and speed; correct result approximately 0.866c.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Stored elastic energy and observable mass
parts.sourceFirstMarkingRisk: Mass-energy equivalence and consequent direction of spring-mass change; negligible magnitude treated as neutral.
